name_note: GTDB and the literature use the same genus name; published work on the genus concerns its species Dolosigranulum pigrum.

sentences.text: Dolosigranulum is a bacterial genus of the human nose and nasopharynx, and its species Dolosigranulum pigrum is described as a commensal isolated from the nasopharynx of healthy children.

In a study of anterior nares swabs collected within 24 hours of delivery, maternal samples were dominated by Corynebacterium and Dolosigranulum, described as genera characteristic of stable, healthy adult nares.
In that same study, newborn samples were instead enriched for Lactobacillus, Burkholderia-Caballeronia-Paraburkholderia, Acinetobacter and Streptococcus.

A report states that specific nasal bacterial genera are differentially associated with respiratory syncytial virus severity in infants, with Dolosigranulum linked to healthy controls or milder outcomes.
In co-culture experiments with pneumococcal strains, Dolosigranulum pigrum and Corynebacterium pseudodiphtheriticum significantly reduced pneumococcal growth, with a synergistic effect when combined.
